## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The MDS MSA criteria paper describes a clinical presentation combining autonomic failure, parkinsonism and cerebellar syndrome in varying combinations. (medium confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.29005 · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD · also: https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/multiple-system-atrophy

## Facts and statements

- [statement] NINDS describes alpha-synuclein buildup in glia as a distinguishing feature of MSA. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/multiple-system-atrophy · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] The MDS MSA criteria paper requires suggestive brain magnetic resonance imaging markers for the clinically established MSA category. (low confidence) — https://movementdisorders.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/mds.29005 · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] NINDS states that levodopa may improve motor function in some people with MSA, although benefits are often short-lived. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/multiple-system-atrophy · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] NINDS identifies tau buildup in affected brain cells as a signature of PSP. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/progressive-supranuclear-palsy · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] NINDS lists trouble looking up or down among the eye and vision symptoms of PSP. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/progressive-supranuclear-palsy · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] The MDS PSP criteria paper identifies ocular motor dysfunction, postural instability, akinesia and cognitive dysfunction as clinical predictor domains. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28467028/ · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] The MDS PSP criteria paper states that earlier NINDS/Society for PSP clinical criteria have excellent specificity but limited sensitivity for variant presentations other than Richardson's syndrome. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28467028/ · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] NINDS describes the cerebral cortex and basal ganglia as the main regions affected by CBD. (low confidence) — https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/disorders/corticobasal-degeneration · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] Alexander and colleagues describe CBD neuropathology as aggregated 4-repeat tau protein isoforms deposited in neurons and glial cells. (low confidence) — https://jnnp.bmj.com/content/85/8/925 · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] Alexander and colleagues distinguish corticobasal syndrome from CBD pathology: patients with similar corticobasal syndromes can have other neurodegenerative pathologies. (low confidence) — https://jnnp.bmj.com/content/85/8/925 · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] The Armstrong consortium criteria paper identifies corticobasal, frontal behavioral-spatial, nonfluent/agrammatic primary progressive aphasia and progressive supranuclear palsy syndromes as CBD phenotypes. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23359374/ · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD
- [statement] The Armstrong consortium proposed more specific probable CBD research criteria; Alexander and colleagues subsequently reported that these criteria did not sufficiently improve diagnostic specificity in their clinicopathological cohort. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23359374/ · keywords: Atypical parkinsonism: MSA, PSP and CBD · also: https://jnnp.bmj.com/content/85/8/925
